Maladaptive Strategies.value: Any form of physical contact with others
push away positive emotions because they feel unsafe
Talking with others about the event or its aftermath

Threat.value: I react with alarm when someone touches me unexpectedly
Unusual silence makes me feel something dangerous is about to happen
I always identify escape routes before I feel comfortable anywhere

Memory.value: I can taste what I tasted during the event when the memory returns
When the memory returns I feel so overwhelmed by emotion that I have to stop
Sometimes I can recall what happened but feel completely numb, as if it happened to a stranger

vignette: Mark, a 36-year-old married North American man and tax consultant, has been struggling with the aftermath of his military service. The traumatic event that haunts him occurred during a patrol in Afghanistan when he was caught in an ambush. As he recounts it, the chaos of gunfire and explosions still resonates vividly, along with the bitter taste of gunpowder lingering on his tongue. Since returning from deployment, Mark has found himself hyper-vigilant and easily startled by sudden movements or unexpected touches-a simple pat on the back at work could send him into a state of intense alarm. This heightened startle response is compounded by unusual silences, which he interprets as ominous signs of impending danger. He always makes sure to identify escape routes whenever he enters a new environment, feeling more secure when he knows how to leave quickly if needed. Mark's reactions are particularly acute in the context of his occupation as a tax consultant. During client meetings, certain conversations that touch on conflict or stressful financial situations can trigger flashbacks. These triggers not only cause him to avoid being touched but also push him away from positive emotions because they feel unsafe and potentially overwhelming. He finds himself avoiding talking about the event altogether, even with his wife, as he fears it will lead to a flood of emotions he feels ill-equipped to handle. When Mark does encounter these triggers in his daily life, his memories come flooding back, often accompanied by vivid sensory details. The taste of gunpowder can return during a flashback, making him feel physically unwell and overwhelming with intense emotion. On other occasions, the memory returns as if it happened to someone else, leaving him feeling numb and disconnected from reality. These memories often lead him to withdraw further into his maladaptive strategies-avoiding touch, pushing away positive emotions, and refusing to talk about what happened. The cycle that Mark is caught in becomes evident through the interactions between these elements. When he encounters triggers such as conflicts or certain conversation topics at work, it leads to overwhelming memories that feel so intense they make him physically ill. This then reinforces his maladaptive strategies-avoiding touch, pushing away positive emotions, and avoiding discussions about the event. Mark's wife has noticed a significant change in his behavior over the past year. He avoids physical affection altogether and is increasingly isolated, even from her. His heightened startle response means that she often walks on eggshells around him, never knowing what might set off an intense reaction. This avoidance of touch and positive emotions has created a rift between them, leading to feelings of isolation and disconnection. The cumulative effect of these maladaptive strategies has taken its toll on Mark's work as well. He avoids social events with clients and colleagues, further isolating himself from the support network he needs. His wife finally encouraged him to seek help when she realized how much his behavior was affecting both their relationship and his professional life. In therapy sessions, Mark is most afraid of losing control and being overwhelmed by emotions or memories that could disrupt his daily functioning again. He hopes for a way to manage these intense reactions without having to isolate himself further from those he loves and the people he works with. Despite feeling stuck in this cycle, he remains determined to find a path forward where he can live more fully and openly. Mark's story is one of a man grappling with profound trauma, trying to navigate his daily life while being haunted by vivid memories and intense reactions that keep him trapped in a cycle of avoidance and fear. His journey towards healing will involve breaking this cycle, finding ways to manage his triggers, and ultimately reconnecting with the world around him.
